QF.id: IV Strategies Using Interest Rate Derivatives_25

question.text: A speculator shorts 100 GOI bond futures contracts at Rs. 103.20 when each contract has a face value of Rs. 2,00,000 (lot size 2,000 units per Rs. 100 face value). Prices fall to Rs. 102.00. What is the total profit before costs?

explanation.text: The Logic: Bond futures prices are quoted per Rs. 100 face value (workbook p. 120). Profit per contract = (103.20 - 102.00)/100 x 2,00,000 = Rs. 2,400. Total = 2,400 x 100 = Rs. 2,40,000. Taking a short futures position is the appropriate stance when bond prices are expected to fall (workbook p. 187). The Trap: Rs. 1,20,000 uses 50 contracts. Rs. 24,000 uses 10 contracts. Rs. 3,60,000 assumes a 1.80 price change. Note: Short futures gain as prices fall, which corresponds to rising yields for bond futures.
